tasks.short: Inspect construction sites for safety and code adherence

steps.what: Inspect and monitor construction sites against safety standards, building codes and specifications

tasks.design: Retain physical inspection and interpretation of site conditions. Approved references in {DOCS} inform the inspection; the energy-service products in the digest do not establish automated construction compliance assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual construction may differ from drawings or conceal important defects.
tasks.enabler_now: Document access supports inspection without replacing on-site judgement.
tasks.still_hard: A visible condition may require further investigation to establish structural or safety significance.
tasks.human_edge: The inspector recognises when evidence is insufficient and directs appropriate follow-up.
tasks.altitude: Inspection time and professional authority stay unchanged.

reach.task: Explain an observed condition requiring specialist assessment

evidence.claim: Retaining contextual site inspection is an E1 assessment from model knowledge; the digest provides no applicable construction-inspection replacement case.

assumptions: Boundary is physical inspection and judgement, excluding daily-log and photograph administration owned by the separate task.
Existing design and code owners supply approved references; no free structured compliant or defect-free flag is presumed.
Retain existing references; no custom inspection system proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes; confirm national building requirements and inspector authority.
unknowns: Inspection scope, applicable codes and specialist support
research_questions: Which observed conditions require specialist investigation before a compliance conclusion?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0; site observation and compliance judgement retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain regulations and recommend remedial actions

steps.what: Confer with owners, violators or authorities to explain regulations and recommend remedial actions

tasks.design: Keep contextual regulatory explanation and remedial discussion with the inspector. Verified findings and requirements in {DOCS} support the conversation; an energy-billing chatbot does not establish suitable building-code advice.
tasks.previous_blocker: The parties need a clear explanation of how requirements apply to actual findings.
tasks.enabler_now: Reference access helps discussion without replacing professional interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Proposed remedies may need design approval or exceed the inspector's authority.
tasks.human_edge: The inspector clarifies uncertainty and recognises when specialist advice is required.
tasks.altitude: Explanation time and remedial recommendation rights stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Retaining contextual regulation and remedy discussions is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is the inspector's discussion, excluding inspection, remedy design, formal enforcement and recipients' implementation labour.
The existing inspection task produces verified findings; regulatory owners supply current texts. No free structured permitted-remedy flag is assumed.
Retain native references; no custom advice system proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes; assign conversations overlapping other inspection tasks once.
unknowns: Delegated authority and permitted recommendation scope
research_questions: Which proposed remedies require an authorised designer or formal authority decision?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0; professional explanation and remedial discussion retain full time.

tasks.short: Maintain daily inspection logs and photographic records

steps.what: Capture daily inspection facts and photographs with explicit record and location associations
Format the daily log and attach selected photographs to the inspection record
Check factual completeness, photo associations and access before filing the inspection record

tasks.design: Configure a native record template in {DOCS} to render captured log fields and explicitly selected photo links. The inspector retains photography, factual capture and exact record review; the system does not infer defects, locations or compliance from images.
tasks.previous_blocker: Daily records require repeated layout and photo attachment work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms and templates can render existing fields and selected attachments.
tasks.still_hard: A correctly attached photograph can omit important context or show the wrong element.
tasks.human_edge: The inspector knows what the photograph actually documents and what is still unobserved.
tasks.altitude: Less record assembly with unchanged factual accountability.

evidence.claim: Template assembly of inspection facts and chosen photographs is an E1 design from model knowledge; the energy-audit digest does not establish this construction-record capability or saving.

assumptions: Boundary is daily log and photographic documentation, excluding the physical inspection and compliance judgement owned by separate tasks.

Inspector s1 produces inspection ID, date, site, element or location ID, factual observation, status explicitly chosen by the inspector, photo ID and caption, photo-to-record link and intended access group. All capture, photography and association choices remain in55 hours.
Missing fields, disputed association or sensitive images return to manual record assembly. Test native forms and attachments before code; no free structured defect code is assumed.
Benefit requires actual separate assembly work; existing automatic filing runtime earns no new labour saving.
unknowns: Actual assembly share, native template support and image access rules
research_questions: Does native assembly save time after capturing fields, checking photographs and correcting associations?

already_counted.description: Facts, photograph capture and explicit association

approvals.approved_version: Exact log version, observations, captions, photo links and access group; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R75 gross25 minus5 upkeep gives net20. E1 manual-assembly scenario; extra captions, corrections and access checks reduce net to3-14 while capture and inspection remain counted.

steps.what: Train, direct or supervise construction inspectors through observed practice and technical feedback

tasks.design: Retain observed instruction and technical supervision. Approved references in {DOCS} support feedback; generated materials do not establish reliable inspection judgement or field technique.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inspection competence requires observing actual evidence gathering and interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Administrative tools do not replace qualified supervision.
tasks.still_hard: A trainee may reach a plausible conclusion from insufficient evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor identifies gaps in observation and reasoning and explains them directly.
tasks.altitude: Training and supervision time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Retaining observed construction-inspector training is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is direct training and supervision, excluding course preparation and trainees' inspection labour.
No free structured competent-inspector flag is assumed.
Current guidance remains; no custom training tool proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes; confirm qualification and supervision requirements locally.
research_questions: Which evidence-gathering errors require field observation rather than document feedback?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0; practical supervision and instruction keep full time.
